### 1 — Scene
A light meal or snack: two whole fruits, jam-covered bread, a small cooked chicken piece, and a single fry.

### 2 — Vessel
A white dinner plate, approximately **26 cm diameter**.  
Plate area = 3.14 × 13² = **531 cm²**.

### 3–7 — Items, area, volume, weight, and energy
The yellow fruit appears to be an Asian pear. Heights below are estimated **average heights across each footprint**, not maximum heights.

| Item | Plate area covered | Area × average height = volume | Density (g/ml) | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Apple | 10% | 53 × 4 = 212 ml | 0.80 | 170 g | 52 | 88 kcal |
| Asian pear | 13% | 69 × 4 = 276 ml | 0.85 | 235 g | 42 | 99 kcal |
| Bread slice | 15% | 80 × 1.3 = 104 ml | 0.30 | 31 g | 265 | 82 kcal |
| Red jam | 0% additional* | 53 × 0.25 = 13 ml | 1.0 | 13 g | 250 | 33 kcal |
| Small cooked chicken piece | 3% | 16 × 1.3 = 21 ml | 0.95 | 20 g | 230 | 46 kcal |
| Single fry | 1% | 5.3 × 0.7 = 3.7 ml | 0.90 | 3 g | 310 | 9 kcal |

*Jam covers approximately 10% of the plate’s area but lies on the bread, so it adds no new covered area. The visible surface allocation is 5% exposed bread + 10% jam-covered bread + 24% other foods = **39%**? Correcting the sum: 10% apple + 13% pear + 15% bread + 3% chicken + 1% fry = **42% total coverage**.

### 8 — Sanity check
Estimated total: **472 g and 357 kcal**. Most of the weight comes from the two whole fruits; the bread and small cooked items contribute comparatively little weight. Fruit identification, plate size, and the chicken’s small bone introduce uncertainty.
